skill.description: Apply the SPARC development methodology with Claude Flow orchestration, TDD workflows, architecture planning, review, and documentation guidance.

skill.author: Claude Flow

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives, not Ruby shell execution. The skill includes NPX command examples, including an alpha tag, which creates supply-chain risk if agents execute them without approval. No prompt injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: NPX examples can execute downloaded package code.
remediation.suggestion: Mark NPX snippets as manual-only and require explicit user approval before agents run them.

remediation.issue: The alpha package tag is not pinned to a reviewed version.
remediation.suggestion: Use a stable pinned claude-flow version in examples or document version verification steps.

remediation.issue: Command safety boundaries are not stated near the workflow examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to review package source, project permissions, and network access before execution.

content.value_statement: Large AI coding projects can lose structure, tests, and review discipline. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through SPARC phases and Claude Flow orchestration.
actual_capabilities: Explains the five SPARC phases from specification through completion.
Lists specialized modes for coding, architecture, testing, review, research, and documentation.
Provides Claude Flow MCP examples for swarm setup, mode execution, monitoring, and memory use.
Describes TDD workflows with red, green, refactor steps and coverage targets.
Shows common workflows for feature development, bug investigation, performance optimization, and pipelines.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow MCP tools or CLI commands for full orchestration.
Does not implement project code by itself; it guides the workflow.
Command examples should be reviewed before execution in any environment.
The methodology can add process overhead for very small tasks.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Break a feature into specification, architecture, tests, implementation, review, documentation, and completion steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Work
use_cases.description: Choose orchestration patterns for research, architecture, coding, testing, and review agents working on one project.

use_cases.title: Improve Delivery Quality
use_cases.description: Use TDD, security review, performance checks, and documentation tasks to reduce late project defects.

prompt_templates.title: Start a SPARC Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use SPARC to plan this feature: [feature]. Include specification, architecture, TDD steps, review, and completion tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Design the Architecture Phase
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the SPARC architecture phase to [project]. Define components, interfaces, data flow, risks, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Create a TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SPARC refinement plan for [feature]. Include failing tests, minimal implementation, refactoring, coverage goals, and reviewer checks.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate a Multi-Agent Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a SPARC multi-agent workflow for [project]. Assign researcher, architect, coder, tester, reviewer, optimizer, and documenter responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Build user authentication for an Express application.
output_examples.output: A phased SPARC plan with requirements, API design, TDD tasks, review checks, documentation work, and completion criteria.
A workflow that analyzes symptoms, reproduces the bug, adds regression tests, applies a fix, and verifies performance.

output_examples.input: Modernize a legacy module without breaking behavior.
output_examples.output: A refactoring plan that creates safety tests, maps dependencies, changes code in increments, and reviews compatibility.

best_practices: Start with clear requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria before implementation.
Use TDD tasks to protect behavior before major refactoring or feature work.
Review command examples and tool permissions before running orchestration workflows.
anti_patterns: Skipping specification and asking agents to code large features immediately.
Running NPX or local commands without checking package source and version.
Using many agents without clear roles, dependencies, and completion criteria.

faq.question: What does SPARC mean?
faq.answer: SPARC means Specification, Pseudocode, Architecture, Refinement, and Completion.

faq.question: Does this skill require Claude Flow?
faq.answer: Claude Flow is required for the documented MCP and CLI orchestration examples.

faq.question: Can I use this with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can follow the methodology, but Claude Flow-specific tool calls may need adaptation.

faq.question: Is this only for large projects?
faq.answer: No. It is most useful for complex tasks, but small features can use a shorter SPARC plan.

faq.question: Does it write production code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions and examples for AI-assisted development.

faq.question: How should teams handle the command examples?
faq.answer: Treat command examples as manual actions. Review packages, versions, and permissions before execution.
